thread:
Maria Suarez: heads up — AcmeRetail (acct: ACME-42) opened a severity-2 ticket about p99 spikes starting ~03:10 UTC. They say users see 6–12s responses intermittently. Attached screenshot of their dashboard.
Tom Nguyen: copying the ticket here — ticket #78932. I pulled our system p95/p99 for the backend routes serving ACME-42, and I do see a p99 jump from ~450ms to 6s around 03:08–03:27. p95 only moved a bit (~550ms -> ~900ms).
Alex Kapoor: thanks. Maria, did they change traffic pattern? any new bursty batched requests or embeddings jobs?
Maria Suarez: they said they rolled a new campaign yesterday but no infra changes. They did say a customer script started calling chat completions in looping batch jobs early this morning — could be noisy.
Tom Nguyen: ok — suspect noisy-neighbor on our multi-tenant pool. I'll check per-tenant concurrency, token counts, and routing.
SRE Oncall Bot: alert: high-tail-latency detected for route /v1/chat/completions (tenant=ACME-42) — p99 5.8s.
Alex Kapoor: immediate triage checklist: 1) check GPU utilization on serving nodes for that tenant 2) examine per-tenant QoS/throttle logs 3) look for hot keys in cache/redis 4) confirm no deploys/rollouts around 03:00
Tom Nguyen: running queries now. Redis slowlog shows a few keys with high read latency from tenant ACME-42 at 03:09. Also saw KV cache miss ratio spike for that tenant's long context workloads.
Tom Nguyen: GPU utilization on pool gpu-pool-5 (where ACME-42 is routed) spiked to 95% at 03:07 and stayed high for ~20m, some hosts hitting OOM kill rates low but present.
Alex Kapoor: are they routed to shared hosted pool or did they have a dedicated reservation?
Maria Suarez: ACME-42 is on hosted standard plan (shared pool) — no dedicated.
Janelle (acct-mgr): they pay for higher-tier support but haven't upgraded to Dedicated. They're pushing for mitigation asap.
Alex Kapoor: probable cause: noisy tenant process from ACME-42 causing resource contention on shared pool (noisy neighbor). Also their requests have larger-than-normal sequence lengths so KV cache pressure and GPU memory use are higher leading to tail latency.
Tom Nguyen: I can confirm per-tenant throttles show ACME-42 hit soft-concurrency limit at 03:05 and started queuing behind other requests. But queueing doesn't explain 6s p99 alone — the GPU saturation and repeated KV misses amplify latency.
Maria Suarez: customer reports user-facing errors occasionally (429 and timeouts).
Alex Kapoor: mitigations to try (short term):
- Move ACME-42 traffic to a different pool (if capacity) or to a less-loaded availability zone
- Apply temporary per-tenant rate-limiter (hard throttle) to cap concurrency and reduce resource shock
- Enable aggressive prefix caching for ACME-42 to reduce KV miss storm
- Rollback any recent customer-side campaign if possible
- If available, spin up a temporary dedicated small reservation for ACME-42 (short-term)
Tom Nguyen: I'm going to 1) add a temporary 20% hard throttle on ACME-42 concurrency, 2) re-route new sessions to gpu-pool-7 with spare capacity, 3) enable aggressive KV caching for their routes. Implementing now.
DeployBot: deploy started: route-change/gpu-pool-7 -> kickoff.
Tom Nguyen: throttle set (concurrency cap = 12) at 03:18 UTC. Routing change in progress — new connections should start landing on gpu-pool-7 within 45s. KV caching policy updated for tenant ACME-42 (prefix caching: aggressive).
SRE Oncall Bot: metric update: p99 for ACME-42 dropped from 5.8s to 1.2s within 2 minutes of routing change. GPU utilization on gpu-pool-5 decreasing.
Maria Suarez: shared with customer: "we’ve applied temporary throttles and shifted new traffic to a less-loaded serving pool. We’re seeing p99 fall to ~1s for your traffic — monitoring for stability. Can you hold any batch jobs for the next hour?"
Janelle (acct-mgr): Acme says they paused the campaign and will monitor. They're okay with temporary throttles but asked for a follow-up with options (dedicated vs reserved capacity).
Alex Kapoor: long-term remediation suggestions to discuss with product/CS:
- Offer proactive per-tenant isolation for high-burst customers (e.g., quick-reservation flow)
- Add tenant-aware autoscale that preemptively moves noisy tenants off shared pools when sustained high-tail is detected
- Improve per-tenant KV cache partitioning or limit backlog of cache-miss storms
- Enhance routing policy to prefer lower-seq-length model variants for noisy tenants automatically
- Add analytics alerting to detect tenant-level token-length anomalies earlier
Tom Nguyen: for the incident notes: root cause = noisy neighbor (ACME-42 batch campaign) causing sustained GPU saturation + KV cache miss storm, exposing multi-tenant tail latency amplification. Mitigations = temporary concurrency throttle, re-route to a less-loaded pool, enable aggressive caching.
Maria Suarez: customer update posted in ticket. They asked for an RCA and what guarantees we can provide. I told them we’ll follow up with a technical postmortem and options for Dedicated.
Alex Kapoor: action items
- Tom: collect relevant logs (GPU metrics, per-tenant throttle events, KV miss ratios, routing decisions) and attach to incident ticket (#78932). ETA 4 hours.
- Alex: draft RCA and recommended product options (Dedicated/reserved + automated tenant move). ETA EOD.
- Maria/Janelle: schedule a customer call for tomorrow 09:00 PDT to review options.
Tom Nguyen: attaching quick grep snippets here for reproducibility and future evals:
```
# query per-tenant p99 from metrics DB
SELECT tenant_id, pctile(0.99)(latency_ms) as p99, time_bucket('1m', ts) as minute
FROM http_requests
WHERE route = '/v1/chat/completions' AND tenant_id = 'ACME-42'
GROUP BY tenant_id, minute
ORDER BY minute DESC
```
```
# check redis slowlog sample
127.0.0.1:6379> SLOWLOG GET 20
1) 1) (integer) 1600000123
   2) (integer) 180
   3) 1) "GET"
      2) "tenant:ACME-42:context:abcdef"
   4) (integer) 1710640000
```
notes: thread contains immediate triage, temporary mitigation (throttle + reroute + caching), follow-up RCA and customer call scheduling.
